Notes: In December 2008, English alternative rock band Keane were said to have been working in the same studio as Kanye, leading to them meeting up and later Tim Rice-Oxley [Keane's keyboardist] and Kanye working on a song together. But there is something – something about cigars that are Cuban. That’s all I can remember! It’s good and maybe it will see the light of day one day."

Name:
Unknown [Madvillainz Collaborations]
(prod. Madvillainz)
Notes: It is heavily implied that Kanye, MF DOOM and Madlib formed a supergroup called Madvillainz in 2009. After MF DOOM's death, rapper J Rocc revealed that Kanye and MF DOOM wanted to form a group called Madvillainz. Kanye's barber Ibn Jasper also said in an Instagram post that he'll always remember the secret studio sessions, implying DOOM and Kanye recorded together. The first Madvillainz remix that released, "Gazillion Ear", featured a Kanye intro. When the Madvillainz remix of "Victory Laps" came out, DOOM's label Lex Records stated that Madvillainz was allegedly made up of Kanye, Madlib, and DOOM. Talib Kweli also tweeted out in 2009 that he was in the studio with Kanye, DOOM and Madlib, although allegedly no music was recorded. It is likely more music came out of the Madvillainz group than just the "Gazillion Ear" and "Victory Lap" remixes and "Disastrous".
Link(s):
Unknown [Madvillainz Collaborations]
(prod. Madvillainz)

Notes: Malik said that originally, "Ghetto University" was "just me and Elton John". Elton John was "on the keys". Contained a Muhammad Ali sample saying, "the champ is here;" which can be heard on versions from the beat copy. Malik attempted to create rhymes around it, but ended up telling the engineer to remove the sample to clear space on the song. After having taken the sample out, he eventually came up with the "all of the lights" part after thinking about his son's first words which were "light". Kanye did not want the track on the album originally, but came convinced over time.

Name:
✨ See Me Again [V1]
(prod. Kanye West)
(Never See Me Again)
Notes: Unfinished track, with some mumble lyrics, leaked from just over a month before My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy dropped. Rumored to be recorded early 2010 for Winter Spring Summer Fall. Was leaked as "Never See Me Again", but current leakers who have the song confirm that the title is "See Me Again". Interpolates "I Never Want To See You Again" by Quasi. This leak gained notable popularity after a widespread theory that it was a "suicide note" of sorts, further influenced by the discovery that the song shared a similar chord progression to "Futari Dake No CEREMONY" by the late J-pop star Yukiko Okada, who comitted suicide in April of 1986 due to alleged relationship issues - which can allude to Kanye's troubles at this time that would result in his breakup with Amber Rose - however this relation has since been debunked and is mostly viewed as a coincidence.

We need to speed that verse up.' Because he's a hip-hop guy, and he's used to doing one beat throughout a song. When I first brought it up, Jeff was livid that I would even want to try something like changing the tempo. But he tried it, and he thought it was terrific, and he loved my slow vocal on the verse - that's my original take on the slow verse, but it's been sped up."

Notes: Dave Tozer said that after hearing this early version, "Kimbra got this idea to try a melody that she had…So she just got on the mic and started humming these melodies. And she did a bunch of that scatting because it was just really about capturing the melody idea she had. And so we got it down and we were like, 'that's cool' and then later as I worked through it…The initial idea was that if we were to use that, we'd probably write some lyrics to it and develop it further. But as I was editing the song and working through it…I just really liked it the way it was…She just sounds so cool. And I started sort of putting it in certain spots and shaping it up so that it was like a reoccurring part, a hook. And then we had this sort of breakdown part, where she's sort of scatting, almost like a solo. And so I just said to John, 'Let's use it like this. I think it's great!'"

(feat. Ty Dolla $ign) (prod. Kanye West, Benji B, Charlie Handsome & Noah Goldstein)
Notes: Initial Charlie Handsome version that was played to Kanye, Rick Rubin. and Post Malone. According to Charlie it has a "really abrasive, high-pitched riser sound" that was played it over the sample chop, "a synth bass mixed in with 808s", "a mic’d recording of a bicycle chain as it spins and slows down" that was used as a hi-hat roll, and "a really interesting chord progression" which they didn’t want. Charlie also said that they just wanted "the riffs, the drums, the 808s—so I cut it in. Where the beat switches up, my parts come in there". Charlie was invited to the studio by Che Pope after Che saw that Post Malone was in the studio writing with Ye, as Charlie works heavily with Post.

Has the rough, unarranged Chance and Kanye vocals, with Justin Bieber's vocals coming in after the beat cuts out. He did not get to record a version separately, as he was handed the mic when the freestyle was happening. The song started as MIKE DEAN playing chords and DJDS in the corner of the room, presumably playing the sample that would later be covered by the choir. Then Swizz Beatz started programming drums, after which Fonzworth Bentley and Plain Pat went to a studio two blocks down and brought tambourines, which they started playing over the song every eight bars. After the instrumental had come together, the freestyle began, with Justin Bieber recording an acapella freestyle after the Chance and Kanye parts which were later cutdown.

According to Fonzworth Bentley, the idea for the second verse came after Fonzworth told Kanye that his brother believes that when the world ends, angels will perpetually come out of waves as they crash down. After being told this, Kanye got Fonzworth and Elon Rutberg (who has a writing credit on release, likely for helping conceptualise the verse) to create an image of this as he is a "visual person". After doing the verse, Kanye changed the album name to Waves, due to what Fonzworth told him and Ye also feeling like the SWISH title "wasnt the best way to communicate what it was that he wanted to communicate". Name:
Ant Clemons - Pootie Tang [V1]
(prod. Bongo ByTheWay & ROBOTSCOTT)
(All Mine, Medulla Oblongata)
Notes:
OG Filename: POOTIE TANG TP ANT BONGO SCOTT
Solo Ant Clemons version. According to xtcy, the file was in a folder of Jeremih and Ant Clemons tracks. According to Ant Clemons in a Rolling Stone article, "the first day [Bongo ByTheWay and I] met we did 11 records". The article later states "Bongo stayed awake for long enough to be impressed with Clemons’ output. He took Clemons to meet Jeremih; West called on Jeremih to come to Wyoming to participate in the sessions for Ye, Jeremih played West a demo with Clemons titled 'All Mine' and West pounced on it". According to Ant Clemons, the song was shown to Ye one week before the album's release. ROBOTSCOTT's release credit likely comes out of courtesy for him being a large contributor to this version of the song and shaping the vision, as none of this production is on release and the stems do not mention him at all. Snippet of what looks to be a scrapped music video posted by Legion on Instagram February 10th, 2018.
